system.name: SimCAS
system.one_liner: Simple framework that lets pre-trained transformers handle long inputs by chunking, aligning chunk boundary tokens and selecting hidden states for decoding.

content.variant_note: parallel chunk streams that share one encoder and exchange [S] and [E] states across chunks, then a chain of token selectors feeding a decoder, with a long feedback line
content.argues: Chunking a long input, aligning [S] and [E] tokens across chunks and selecting hidden states keeps cost linear while the decoder still draws on the whole input.
content.subject: Chunked encoder input with BOS/EOS alignment, sequential token selectors, and a decoder that cross-attends to selected tokens, with feedback.

elements.name: Shared self-attention
elements.role: the same self-attention applied to every chunk
elements.drawn_as: beige rounded box per chunk with an ellipsis between

elements.name: BOS Alignment
elements.role: averages the [S] hidden states of all chunks and writes the result back to each (paper text)
elements.drawn_as: white rounded box with red outline, thin red arrows in from each [S] and out to each [S]

elements.name: EOS Alignment
elements.role: averages the [E] hidden states of all chunks and writes the result back to each (paper text)

elements.name: Sequential Select
elements.role: stage that picks the most representative hidden states chunk by chunk
elements.drawn_as: light-blue tinted band with a rotated teal title

elements.name: Token Selector (x3)
elements.role: selects tokens of one chunk, given the state carried from the previous selection
elements.drawn_as: white rounded box with orange outline per chunk, candidate row below and selected row above

elements.name: Selected Tokens
elements.role: all selected tokens collected for the decoder
elements.drawn_as: vertical strip of dashed squares with rotated labels ([S]^0, 2, 3, 5, 6, [E]_2, dots, N-2, N)

elements.name: K, V
elements.role: the selected tokens enter the decoder cross-attention as keys and values
elements.drawn_as: label under an arrow into Cross-attention

elements.name: Decoder Layer (N2 x)
elements.role: standard decoder layer stack
elements.drawn_as: pale yellow tinted column with title and N2 x at the top

elements.name: Masked Self-attention
elements.role: decoder self-attention over the decoder input
elements.drawn_as: teal rounded box

elements.name: Cross-attention
elements.role: attends to the selected tokens
elements.drawn_as: salmon rounded box with K, V arrow in and a line out to the feedback

elements.name: Feed-Forward Layer
elements.role: decoder feed-forward block
elements.drawn_as: light green rounded box

elements.name: Add & Norm (x3)
elements.role: residual and normalisation after each decoder sub-block

elements.name: Decoder Input (M tokens)

layout.arrangement_note: Left, bottom-up: the encoder input strip with a brace, chunked rows, a grey Encoder Layers band (self-attention boxes at its foot, BOS and EOS alignment boxes crossing its middle) and a light-blue Sequential Select band on top with a chain of three token selectors. At the right a yellow Decoder Layer column built bottom-up above the decoder input, a thin Selected Tokens strip between the two, and a long feedback line running along the top edge.

encoding.color_means: One colour per chunk is kept from the input strip through every row to the selected tokens (pink, purple, green); grey = start tokens [S], white = end tokens [E]; red = BOS alignment, blue = EOS alignment; orange outline = token selector; light-blue squares = decoder input; band tints: grey = encoder layers, light blue = selection, pale yellow = decoder layer.
encoding.line_style_means: Dashed boxes = candidate or selected tokens and the logits; solid thick arrows = data flow; thin red and blue arrows = BOS and EOS alignment flows; the long black return line = feedback.
encoding.shape_means: Small squares = tokens; rounded rectangles = modules; white rounded boxes with a coloured outline = the new operations (alignment, token selector); braces = length of an input sequence.
encoding.marker_means: Subscripts and superscripts index chunks ([S]_1, [E]_2, [S]^k); N1 x and N2 x give layer counts; numbers are token positions.
encoding.emphasis: The new operations are the only white boxes with coloured outlines and sit on tinted bands, while the standard transformer parts are pastel filled.

lessons.what_to_learn: Show token-level mechanics by carrying one colour per chunk through every row of numbered squares and singling out special tokens (grey start, white end) so coloured arrow bundles can show how information crosses chunks; put the new operations in white boxes with coloured outlines on tinted bands.
lessons.suits: Sequence-processing methods that cut inputs into pieces and exchange or select information across them: long-context, memory, compression and token-pruning papers.

The decoder output logits and attention scores are utilized as rewards for updating the token selector.

summary: SimCAS lets off-the-shelf pre-trained transformers process long inputs in three steps: chunk, align and select. Figure 1 is read bottom-up on the left. The N input tokens are cut into chunks (one colour per chunk) and each chunk receives [S], [P] and [E] tokens; the chunks run through shared self-attention in a grey encoder band, where BOS and EOS alignment boxes with red and blue arrows exchange the [S] and [E] states between chunks. A light-blue Sequential Select band uses a chain of token selectors to pick tokens, which go as K, V to the cross-attention of a yellow decoder layer stack on the right. A long line labelled Output Feedback and Attention Feedback returns from the decoder to the selectors.
summary_zh: SimCAS 处理长输入：切块、对齐、选择。图 1 自下而上：输入切成彩色块并补 [S][P][E]，BOS/EOS 对齐交换块间信息，Token Selector 选出隐藏状态作 K、V 送入解码器，顶部长线为反馈。
